notes: Search tool hit the usage limit on the 14th call (13 calls returned results). NICE NG111 hospital-referral: the first pass overstated it. NG111 (visual summary/recommendations as returned) says refer adults aged 16+ with symptoms or signs of a more serious illness such as sepsis, and only CONSIDER referral/specialist advice for pregnancy, significant dehydration or inability to take oral fluids/medicines, or higher complication risk; babies under 3 months go to a paediatric specialist (via NG224). The final text now says this correctly and no longer says pregnant/dehydrated adults 'are referred'. The returned NG111 pages were partly draft versions, so the under-3-months/IV wording was dropped. Return-to-work 'up to 2 weeks' is on the NHS treatment page (kept); 'older people may take longer' came from the NHS 111 Wales page, not nhs.uk, and is attributed that way (not added to references, to avoid a non-core host). Prevention habits: the NHS UTI page returned water, wiping front to back, not holding urine and low-dose antibiotics for recurrent UTIs; voiding after sex and treating constipation came only from NHS trust leaflets, so they are attributed to 'NHS hospital leaflets'; the main nhs.uk kidney-infection page could not be confirmed to carry a prevention section (NHS UTI page added to references). Risk factors: NIDDK returned women, pregnancy, recent bladder infection, urinary blockage (stone, enlarged prostate), vesicoureteral reflux (children), repeat infections, diabetes, kidney disease, sickle cell disease; 'childhood and older age', immune-suppression examples and 'poorly controlled' diabetes were not returned and were cut. Removed ibuprofen from the medications links (sources only say it is not normally recommended); paracetamol kept. Urgency wording now names 999/A&E, NHS 111 and urgent/routine GP routes in seekCare and section 6; the NHS statement for children is a blended-summary attribution (urgent GP or NHS 111 for a child who may have a kidney infection) and the exact NHS wording could not be re-checked after the search limit. Alias: 'pyelonephritis' is also an alias of urinary-tract-infection (aliases UTI, cystitis, pyelonephritis, bladder infection); check_batch.py did not flag it, but the maintainer may want to drop it from the UTI page so search is not ambiguous. Article block is ~1216 words (sections 129-181 words, faqs 55-64). Textbook: 1 of the first-pass sentences (flank definition).
